item.title: Texas to play Ole Miss without Colin Simmons and possibly Hollywood Smothers
item.description: Trainers check on Texas edge Colin Simmons (1) after an injury during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) When it plays Ole Miss on Saturday, the Texas football team will be without one starter. But will that number swell to two? On Thursday, Texas had two significant notes on its SEC-mandated availability report. First, the Longhorns ruled that Colin Simmons won't play against the Rebels. Texas also downgraded Hollywood Smothers' status to "doubtful." More: Subscribe to the Statesman's Texas sports newsletter Simmons, who leads the country with his 10.5 sacks, was initially given a "doubtful" designation on Wednesday's availability report. Him joining freshman edge rusher Richard Wesley on the sidelines, though, isn't a huge surprise. After leaving the fourth quarter of Saturday's game with what Texas had described as a leg injury, it was reported by several outlets that Simmons may miss several weeks. View this post on Instagram A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom) A fourth-year running back, Smothers was labeled as "questionable" on Wednesday. Despite missing last month's game at Tennessee, Smothers has rushed for a team-high 289 yards this season . On Wednesday, Texas also listed receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman as "questionable." Freshman running back Derrek Cooper is considered "probable" for this weekend. Texas (4-2, 1-2) will be looking to snap a two-game losing streak and stay in the hunt for a College Football Playoff berth when it hosts Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) at Royal-Memorial Stadium on Saturday night . Ole Miss and UT are respectively ranked seventh and 19th in the Associated Press' poll. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at Texas to play Ole Miss without Colin Simmons and possibly Hollywood Smothers .

item.title: 🔥 After penalty drama! The Libertadores-2026 final is set
item.description: 🔥 After penalty drama! The Libertadores-2026 final is set Often criticized for his many mistakes throughout his career, 40-year-old Muslera secured a "Maracanazo" of his own. He saved THREE Flamengo penalties on Thursday night (22). And sent Estudiantes through to the Libertadores final against Palmeiras. After knocking out Corinthians in Itaquera, the Argentine side did the same to Flamengo at the Maracanã itself, in front of more than 70,000 fans. Preventing a third final between the Rio club and Palmeiras. After a goalless draw in Argentina, Estudiantes created big chances, went down to ten men and held on for another 0-0 draw. Then watched their goalkeeper deny Jorginho, Paquetá and Bruno Henrique to seal a 3-2 shootout win. Los Pincharratas also prevented Brazilian football from already securing an eighth straight Libertadores title. Another all-Brazilian final would have seen the country overtake Argentina in tournament titles. It remains 25 apiece until November 28. Estudiantes turn up the heat as Rossi takes center stage The Argentine side came out all guns blazing from the start. And began controlling proceedings after escaping at least two yellow cards. Rossi had to come to the rescue twice in the same minute. He saved Rojo's effort inside the box and then stretched at full length to deny Rodríguez. Pedro managed to create Flamengo's best chance in the 33rd minute. But Leonardo Jardim's side went into halftime without testing Muslera—just as in the first leg. Estudiantes down to 10 men 🟥 Gustavo Tejera drew attention in the first half for being "stingy" with his cards. But he came back from the break a "different" referee. And Baltasar Rodríguez, already on a yellow, picked up another five minutes into the second half. Despite their numerical advantage, Flamengo still struggled to break into the opposition box. Credit to opponents who stayed compact without the ball. And sat even deeper after losing a player. Arrascaeta, returning from a fracture, was Flamengo's first change. Three substitutions at once followed. And a more attacking Flamengo. And Plata was denied by Muslera with his very first chance. Flamengo managed to apply some pressure. But could not overcome opponents who defended successfully without the ball. Muslera makes THE DIFFERENCE Jorginho had been UNSTOPPABLE from the penalty spot. But he became the Uruguayan's first victim. Paquetá was also denied by Muslera. And Bruno Henrique, who had to score, suffered the same fate. Estudiantes missed just one—Cetré blazed his over. And they did not even need to take their final kick. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Live Coverage: Patriots look for comeback in final quarter vs. Bears
item.description: The New England Patriots made a quick return to the field Thursday night and look to continue the win streak against the Bears. The Patriots struggled to get much going against Chicago, but Rhamondre Stevenson got his team within a score with a big touchdown run to end the first half. Follow along with MassLive for live Patriots-Bears updates. FOURTH QUARTER UPDATES 14:48 — Bears are called for an illegal shift on their first drive of the fourth quarter. It’s 1st-and-15. 15:00 — The Patriots begin the final quarter with a false start penalty. New England will punt. THIRD QUARTER UPDATES END OF THIRD QUARTER Bears 27, Patriots 21 3:03 — The Patriots defense needed a big drive and they got it. Chicago goes three-and-out. SCORE UPDATE: Bears 27, Patriots 21 Drake Maye connects with Eli Raridon for 30 yards and the rookie tight end brings the Patriots within a score. The extra point is good. 8:10 — Drake Maye somehow gets the first down after scrambling and keeping the play alive. He finds Hunter Henry to continue the drive. SCORE UPDATE: Bears 27, Patriots 14 9:41 — Colston Loveland breaks a tackle and gets into th end zone for a Bears touchdown. The extra point is good. 10:18 — Caleb Williams is just short of a first down after a run. It’s 2nd-and-1. 10:30 — The Bears are inching closer to the end zone. 13:44 — Caleb Williams uses his legs to pick up a first down for the Bears. HALFTIME Bears 20, Patriots 14 SECOND QUARTER UPDATES SCORE UPDATE: Bears 20, Patriots 14 That was quick. Drake Maye connects with Rhamondre Stevenson, who takes it 48 yards to the house to get the Patriots back in the game before halftime. SCORE UPDATE: Bears 20, Patriots 7 Luther Burden continues to torch New England. His 24-yard touchdown puts Chicago up by two scores ahead of halftime. The extra point is good. 0:21 — Bears take a timeout on 3rd down. 2:09 — Another penalty by the Patriots. Gabe Jacas with a late hit on Caleb Williams. 2:50 — The Patriots defense appears to bail out the offense and force the Bears to three-and-out. But Charles Woods is called for holding and it’s first down. 3:25 — Brutal. Drake Maye is intercepted in the end zone. 4:10 — Drake Maye gets 10 yards and then some as he moves the Patriots down the field. 6:48 — Efton Chism’s first grab of the night gets the Patriots a first down with a 16-yard catch-and-run. INJURY UPDATE: SCORE UPDATE: Bears 13, Patriots 7 7:04 — Three more for Chicago after another field goal. 7:30 — That’s a new one. The Bears hand the ball off to guard Joe Thuney and are called for illegal forward handing. 8:51 — Going for it paid off. The Bears get about 8 yards thanks to D’Andre Swift. 9:11 — The Bears are going for it on 4th-and-inches. INJURY UPDATE: Kevin Byard is down and getting looked at by the trainers. He jogged off the field and into the blue medical tent. 11:26 — A 47-yard kick return for the Bears coupled with a 5-yard illegal formation penalty by the Patriots puts Chicago at the 43-yard line. SCORE UPDATE: B

item.title: How to watch Miami Hurricanes vs Pittsburgh Panthers in Week 8
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA OCTOBER 17: Miami Hurricanes mascot Sebastian the Ibis gives thumbs up during the game against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium on October 17, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images To continue the 2026 season, the Miami Hurricanes continue the homestand with another game at Hard Rock Stadium. Coming to town to step up onto the big stage to play the Hurricanes are the Pittsburgh Panthers. For Miami, they look to continue the season with a win and get back to the standard of performance we’ve seen for the majority of the last 2 seasons that was sorely lacking last week vs FSU. For Pittsburgh, they look to right the ship after consecutive losses after their star QB Mason Heintschel went down for the year with a torn ACL. They face a tall task, to be sure. Here are the particulars for you to watch this week’s game: Florida State Seminoles (5-2, 2-2 ACC) at #1 Miami Hurricanes (6-0, 4-0 ACC) Game Day: October 24th Kickoff time : 12:00pm Eastern TV : ESPN Online Stream : WatchESPN/ESPN+ Streaming : You can catch college football games with SlingTV , which offers day, week and weekend passes. Check it out! Radio : 560 WQAM , 990AM ESPN Deportes , WVUM , TuneIn app has a channel for CFB broadcasts , which may help you as well. FanDuel Sportsbook odds : Open: Miami -22.5, O/U 52.5; as of 10pm Thursday: Miami -20.5, O/U 48.5 Every game for Miami is a big game, and this is another spotlight game for the Canes. Everybody who loves Miami, and many who HATE Miami, will be tuned in, watching and dissecting every play. And with Pitt players and coaches talking plenty of trash heading into this game, there’s bound to be some animus, and I can’t wait to see what Miami does to address such disrespect. This is another week where Miami will showcase their immense talent and skill. After their worst performance of the year last week — even in a win — the Canes will look to right the ship, get back on track and play to the standard, and dispatch Pitt and their loudmouth coach while doing wo. See you at HRS on Saturday at high noon! Go Canes

item.title: Tom Izzo Unloads on Trey Kaufman-Renn’s Sixth-Year Ruling
item.description: Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo spoke to the media Thursday in a video posted by SpartanMag , and he did not spare the eligibility fights reshaping college basketball. Izzo said there is always a positive and a negative when the rules change, and that the NCAA’s new age-based eligibility rule cuts both ways for a coach. What he likes about it is that it should end cases like Trey Kaufman-Renn’s, the former Purdue forward who won a court order for a sixth year and is now practicing at Kansas . “What I like about it is no more BS on the phony stuff,” Izzo said. “Like, I heard the guy in Kansas, I mean, from Purdue, is a joke. Joke, nice kid. Just a joke. What a joke.” Tom Izzo Blames the Lawyers, Not the Players Izzo was careful about where he aimed it. He has already called the transfer portal detrimental to kids , and he made a similar point Thursday about the players caught in the eligibility cases. The people he holds responsible are the ones filing the paperwork. “Tough for him, too, because it’s like you’re just playing by whatever the rules are, right?” Izzo said. “And it’s like, is it him? Is it the powers that be? Lawyers. It’s lawyers.” Trey Kaufman-Renn’s Sixth Year, Explained Kaufman-Renn spent five years at Purdue. He played the past four seasons after sitting out 2021-22 as a redshirt , a year Purdue says was derailed by a knee injury in early November that required surgery. A judge granted him a sixth year of eligibility in his lawsuit against the NCAA, and he secured an injunction last week. Kansas coach Bill Self announced Monday that Kaufman-Renn had enrolled in classes and was practicing with the Jayhawks, taking the last roster spot after freshman Grant Mordini suffered a season-ending patellar tendon injury in September. The backlash followed him because the Minnesota Timberwolves drafted him in the second round and he was on the team’s summer league roster in Las Vegas. In late August the Big 12 announced a ban on former professional athletes returning to college, telling programs they cannot roster an athlete who declared for a pro draft without withdrawing in time, was listed on a professional roster, or signed a professional contract. Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark said Kaufman-Renn is different because he never formally declared. “He was automatically put in the draft,” Yormark said Tuesday. “He didn’t declare for the draft. That is the distinction, just so you know.” Kaufman-Renn’s attorneys said during the case that he never signed his contract with the Timberwolves. Jaxon Kohler’s Case Is Similar Former Michigan State forward Jaxon Kohler is on a parallel track. He transferred to BYU this past offseason after playing for the Utah Jazz’s summer league team , and he is one of 76 plaintiffs, most of them from the 2022 recruiting class, challenging the NCAA’s age-based model in Glancey v. For the Patriots, much of that adversity was self-inflicted. While the team has been hit by significant injuries, Drake Maye and the offense severely underperformed in the early weeks of the season. They have since turned it around and won three consecutive games, positioning themselves as legitimate AFC East contenders. The Bears, meanwhile, have started three different quarterbacks through six weeks after a hamstring injury sidelined Caleb Williams for three games. Williams returned for last week's win over the Falcons , and he clearly made an impact on the offense. item.title: Bruins Answer Quiet Dallas Finish With 6-0 Statement Against Predators
item.description: Bruins Answer Quiet Dallas Finish With 6-0 Statement Against Predators originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Bruins did not need long to show how they planned to respond to Tuesday’s overtime loss. Boston was held without a shot for the final 12:43 of regulation and overtime in a 3-2 defeat to the Dallas Stars. On Thursday night, the Bruins scored twice in each period, got a 28-save shutout from Michael DiPietro and rolled past the Nashville Predators, 6-0. That contrast made the victory more than a welcome return to the win column. Boston played with the pace and attacking pressure that had gone missing late against Dallas, while backing it up with a defensive performance that gave Nashville little room to recover. Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring 3:49 into the game, finishing a cross-ice pass from David Pastrnak. Elias Lindholm doubled Boston’s lead with a power-play deflection late in the first period. The Bruins had an early cushion, but the defining sequence came in the second. A SIX-PACK SHUTOUT 👌 https://t.co/OoS3asLXW4 — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 23, 2026 With Boston leading 2-0, DiPietro made a key stop on Nashville’s Mavrik Bourque. Pastrnak then scored at the other end to make it 3-0, turning a chance for the Predators to make the game interesting into another step toward a rout. MORE : Bruins vs. Predators Score, Highlights From NHL Game: Boston Blanks Nashville 6-0 Can't Stop, Won't Stop The Bruins kept coming. JJ Peterka made it 4-0 before the second intermission, and Mark Kastelic and Pastrnak added third-period goals. Pastrnak finished with two goals and two assists, while Charlie McAvoy recorded four assists. The six-goal performance was the obvious change from Tuesday. The less flashy difference was Boston’s ability to protect its advantage. DiPietro stopped all 28 shots he faced, and the Bruins never let Nashville turn a promising moment into sustained pressure. Boston had gone 3-0-1 on its four-game road trip before the overtime loss in Dallas. Thursday’s win moved the Bruins’ unbeaten run in regulation to seven games, at 6-0-1, and offered a far more convincing response than simply scraping out another close result. A 6-0 score can make a game look easy. The Bruins’ answer to Dallas showed what changed: they kept attacking, and they finished the night by shutting the door. item.description: For a second time this season, the New England Patriots will appear on national television on Thursday night. The hope is that the outcome will be different than the last time. After dropping the season opener to the Seattle Seahawks, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will now take on the Chicago Bears in a battle of 4-2 teams. With both clubs on a short week and facing some personnel questions, proper physical and mental preparation was one of the key talking points during the week. “You can’t let how you feel physically affect your mental preparation,” said Vrabel. “It’s something that we’ve tried to focus on during these short weeks over the last however many years that we’ve done them.” Will the Patriots’ preparation help them earn a fifth victory? Let’s find out together. Welcome to our Patriots-Bears live tracker and community discussion. Brown’s head. Drake Maye found more success targeting his running backs, hitting Rhamondre Stevenson for a gain of 19 yards and later finding TreVeyon Henderson on back-to-back plays. However, a Stevenson run on 3rd-and-6 didn’t get the proper yards and New England turned the ball over on downs after a sack on the subsequent 4th-and-5. The Bears offense started its Thursday night in good field position, and with a chunk play to Luther Burden for 26 yards against Marcus Jones. item.content:encoded: For a second time this season, the New England Patriots will appear on national television on Thursday night. The hope is that the outcome will be different than the last time. After dropping the season opener to the Seattle Seahawks, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will now take on the Chicago Bears in a battle of 4-2 teams. With both clubs on a short week and facing some personnel questions, proper physical and mental preparation was one of the key talking points during the week. “You can’t let how you feel physically affect your mental preparation,” said Vrabel. “It’s something that we’ve tried to focus on during these short weeks over the last however many years that we’ve done them.” Will the Patriots’ preparation help them earn a fifth victory? Let’s find out together. Welcome to our Patriots-Bears live tracker and community discussion. Live score: Patriots 21 : 27 Bears Thursday, Oct. 22, 8:15 p.m. ET | Soldier Field (Chicago, IL) | Broadcast information | Game day roster | Inactives | Weather forecast First quarter The Patriots started the game on offense, and with an incompletion that sailed high over wide receiver A.J. Brown’s head. Drake Maye found more success targeting his running backs, hitting Rhamondre Stevenson for a gain of 19 yards and later finding TreVeyon Henderson on back-to-back plays. However, a Stevenson run on 3rd-and-6 didn’t get the proper yards and New England turned the ball over on downs after a sack on the subsequent 4th-and-5. The Bears offense started its Thursday night in good field position, and with a chunk play to Luther Burden for 26 yards against Marcus Jones. However, an inaccurate pass on a subsequent 3rd-and-7 ended the drive and set up a 43-yard field goal for the game’s first points. | Patriots 0 : 3 Bears The Patriots offense went nowhere on its second possession. After two short runs to start the series, quick pressure off another Bears blitz look forced a throw off the mark and Mitch Wishnowsky punt. Chicago’s offense did not fare much better, answering with a three-and-out-of its own. Two short runs set up a 3rd-and-6. A short Caleb Williams pass to D’Andrew Swift gained no yards thanks to Charles Woods and Christian Elliss quickly bringing down the ball carrier. Drake Maye and company, meanwhile, went three-and-out in a similar fashion on their next series: a short Corey Kiner run was followed by two negative plays, including DeMario Douglas losing a yard on 3rd-and-8. After neither offense managed to do much on the last few drives, the Bears not only gained a first down again but then beat the Patriots defense on a 58-yard catch-and-run to Luther Burden against a coverage bust involving Christian Elliss and Charles Woods. The play set the home team up with a 1st-and-goal at the 4-yard line, and it took D’Andre Swift just one play to find the end zone for the first touchdown of the night. | Patriots 0 : 10 Bears Deciding to focus more on the passing game to start the next drive, the Patriots finally picked up a first down again when Drake Maye connected with Eli Raridon for again of 15 to close out Quarter 1. Second quarter New England kept moving the chains to open the second period, driving into Bears territory for the first time all game. A 16-yard pass to Hunter Henry and a 13-yard run by Rhamondre Stevenson then set up a goal-to-go situation, with Drake Maye capping the series on a touchdown scramble from 7 yards out. Maye initially was ruled down short of the goal line, but Mike Vrabel successfully challenged the spot and was rewarded with seven points. | Patriots 7 : 10 Bears Drake Maye reaches for the score 🙌 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/GvRdrWHNp5 — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 Momentum quickly shifted back Chicago’s way after Drake Maye’s touchdown. The team started its next series with a 47-yard kickoff return, and thanks to a tagged-on penalty found itself on the New England side of the field right away. The Patriots did get a chance to stop the Bears on 4th-and-inches shortly thereafter, but D’Andre Swift moved the chains. However, back-to-back penalties against the Bears — including one negating a 2-yard Joe Thuney run — ended the series with a field goal. | Patriots 7 : 13 Bears New England started its next drive with a 16-yard pass to Efton Chism, and a couple of good Corey Kiner runs plus an Eli Raridon catch and Drake Maye scramble later found itself in the red zone. However, the opportunity went to waste when Maye was intercepted on an attempted end zone pass for Raridon. The Patriots kept hurting themselves on the next drive. A Charles Woods hold negated a third down stop, while Gabe Jacas was flagged for roughing the passer to help the Bears get into field goal range again. New England did find itself in a favorable position on a 3rd-and-17 after a Marcus Jones sack, but Luther Burden again managed to make a big play when he took a short pass 24 yards into the end zone for a touchdown. | Patriots 7 : 20 Bears The Patriots had only nine seconds on the clock, and they made them count. First, Drake Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards, before finding Rhamondre Stevenson with three seconds left.The veteran running back took a short pass 48 yards into the end zone as time ran out on the second quarter. | Patriots 14 : 20 Bears RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 Third quarter Starting the second half on defense, the Patriots were in a position for a quick three-and-out but surrendered a conversion to a scrambling Caleb Williams. A pair of short passes to D’Andre Swift allowed the Bears to set up shop in New England territory again, and not just that: they capped their nine-play, 72-yard drive with Colston Loveland breaking a tackle on a 12-yard touchdown. | Patriots 14 : 27 Bears The Patriots could have answered with a big play right on the next drive, but a deep pass intended for A.J. Brown was broken up at the catch point. The pair did connect later on the series to pick up 16 yards. That play plus a pair of completions to Hunter Henry allowed New England to return into field goal range. The team’s ambition went beyond three points, though, and it capped the drive accordingly when Drake Maye hit Eli Raridon for a 30-yard touchdown. | Patriots 21 : 27 Bears Drake Maye DIME to Eli Raridon 🪙 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/ajUvbcD8Oo — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 23, 2026 After taking some hits the last few drives, the Patriots delivered a big three-and-out following their touchdown to Eli Raridon. A short pass followed by two incompletions — prompted by the defensive front generating some pressure — allowed the ball to return to New England via punt. That punt was fielded by Marcus Jones at the 7-yard line and returned 19 yards to improve what would have been some bad starting field position. The Patriots managed to get the ball out even further but right before the end of the quarter found themselves 2 yards short after a Drake Maye third-down scramble near midfield. Fourth quarter The Patriots started the fourth quarter intending to go for it on 4th-and-2, but a false start penalty against Matt Pryor cost them 5 yards and brought out the punt team. Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! item.title: Kings 3, Islanders 2 (OT): Isles rally but Clarke scores winner
item.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 22: Victor Eklund #38 of the New York Islanders (c) celebrates his second period goal against the Los Angeles Kings at UBS Arena on October 22, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a really impressive effort from the New York Islanders tonight after going down 2-0 in the first period. Semyon Varlamov wasn’t at his sharpest tonight; both shots that Artemi Panarin got past him weren’t great. But the Isles responded well, especially in the second period, which they controlled offensively in a way we haven’t seen yet this season. It just took a long time to get anything past Darcy Kuemper. Victor Eklund broke Kuemper’s shutout with a power play goal, and then Matthew Schaefer picked up his first of the season to tie the game. That goal also tied him with Bobby Orr for second-most goals by a teenage defenseman, so no big deal there or anything. Eklund had a really strong game overall, and he’s looking more and more like he fits in the NHL with each game he plays. It’s also extremely funny to see him looking like a little kid out there and taking down big guys like Konstas Helenius. I hope he really starts stringing these good performances together, it’d be awesome to have another young talent take big steps forward. Unfortunately, the Isles came up short in overtime. They definitely miss Mat Barzal in 3 on 3 situations. There’s no one on the team that can replace his skillset in general, but it’s especially noticeable in OT. They still picked up a point, and they’ve got points in their last five games, and have still looked solid despite all the injuries up front. Just a minute later, Artemi Panarin opened the scoring from a tough angle on a shot Semyon Varlamov probably wants back. Emil Heineman’s backhand shot was stopped by Darcy Kuemper right after. Victor Eklund won the puck along the boards from Konstas Helenius and set up a great chance, with Matt Kessel’s shot getting behind Kuemper. Mikey Anderson had to dive behind him to stop that shot from crossing the line. Unfortunately, right after that great shift, Panarin picked up his second of the night on another shot Varlamov probably should’ve had, putting the Isles in a 2-0 hole towards the end of the first. Bo Horvat went to the box for hooking, but then Drew Doughty took a shot at Matthew Schaefer, which led to Logan Stanley fighting Konstas Helenius. Near the end of the period, Varlamov saved shots from Panarin and Doughty to keep just the two goal deficit heading into the second. Second Period The Islanders dominated the whole period, outshooting the Kings 17-9, but couldn’t get anything past Kuemper for most of the period. Heineman and Eklund got a 2 on 1, but the pass option was taken away by Brian Dumoulin and Heineman ran out of time to do anything interesting with the puck. Brayden Schenn tipped a shot off the post, and Simon Holmstrom had a chance in the slot but Kuemper got the save. Schaefer took down Adrian Kempe on a breakaway and Kempe was rewarded a penalty shot, which Varlamov crucially saved. Heineman was tripped by Dumoulin a couple minutes after that, and on that power play, Victor Eklund took a shot that trickled past Kuemper to make it 2-1. View Link Jared Wright got tangled up with Schaefer, and they both went to the box late, for holding and hooking respectively. Third Period The Isles didn’t quite keep up the pace from the second period into the third. Varlamov needed to be sharp, making a few critical saves when needed. Then, 7 minutes into the period, Schenn passed the puck off to Stanley, who found Schaefer with space, and Schaefer scored his first goal of the season to tie the game. View Link Despite putting up 42(!!) shots on Kuemper in regulation, the Isles couldn’t find the go ahead goal, and so we went off to overtime for the first time this season at UBS Arena. OT Bo Horvat’s shot was saved by Kuemper, but once the Kings got possession, they never really gave it up. Adrian Kempe had a great chance saved by Varlamov, but Brandt Clarke put the winner home for LA in a game the Islanders really should have picked up two points from. Up Next Next, the Islanders head out to Dallas to take on the Stars on Sunday, October 25, kicking off a three game road trip around the Central Division.

item.title: Freshman helps DeWitt boys soccer upset Eastern for district title
item.description: DeWITT — The playing opportunities haven't always been there this fall for Jake Wever. But the freshman forward has bought into his role and been willing to do what the DeWitt boys soccer team has needed him to do this fall. And that has led to some good results. That included Thursday, Oct. 22 as Wever came through on a big stage to help the Panthers extend their season Wever scored a goal in the 20th minute for DeWitt in its 1-0 victory over No. 3-ranked Eastern in a Division 2 district final on its home field. "He's a freshman that doesn't look like a freshman and didn't play like a freshman today," DeWitt coach Joe Ishraidi said of Wever. "He came through when we needed him. He hasn't always played the most minutes but he's played important minutes . He was there when we needed it and did what we talked about and put it in the back of the net." More: Michigan high school boys soccer: See Greater Lansing district results The district championship was the second straight for the Panthers and seventh in eight seasons for the program. Wever was pleased to play a role in DeWitt (11-4-5) adding another layer to its postseason success and advancing to next week's regional where it will face Bay City Western at Swartz Creek. "It feels great," Wenver said.. "(The goal) means like more than myself. (This was) for all the seniors that are leaving this year. Putting one in just to win a district championship and with the home crowd and probably our biggest fan section of the year (was great)." The victory marked the third straight shutout for goalkeeper Vince Rose and DeWitt, which opened district play with a 2-0 win over Haslett and followed with a 1-0 semifinal win over Mason on Oct. 19. "They did everything we talked about," Ishraidi said. "They believed in each other, they fought for each other and I'm happy for them that they got to see the fruits of their labor tonight." DeWitt knocked off Eastern in a district final for a second straight season. The loss ended a historic season for Eastern, which won the CAAC Red title and finished as the CAAC Gold Cup champion. The Quakers close the season 17-2-3. Contact Brian Calloway at bcalloway@lsj.com. Follow him on X @brian_calloway. This article originally appeared on Lansing State Journal: Freshman helps DeWitt boys soccer upset Eastern for district title

item.title: Texas HC Steve Sarkisian drops ‘edgy’ truth bomb on Arch Manning
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Texas HC Steve Sarkisian drops ‘edgy’ truth bomb on Arch Manning appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas football is facing mounting tensions to address its quarterback position. Yes, that involves fans hoping Arch Manning lands on the bench. Sounds like coach Steve Sarkisian is riding with Manning for the Ole Miss showdown , though. Sarkisian even dropped an “edgy” truth bomb about how his QB is, arguably, the most talked about player in America . “I would use the word edgy, and I like it. He’s edgy right now. And I think that somebody texted me today that we lost the ‘Aw Shucks’ kid and we created something else,” Sarkisian began via Tyler Horka of On3/Rivals Thursday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But Sark downplays that Texas has lost Manning during this struggling state. “I don’t know if we lost him. We created this. We did. All of us. Y’all included. Me. The whole thing, right? Everybody on ESPN, we’ve created this. And so we’ll see what comes out of it,” Sarkisian said. Another words, Sarkisian is acknowledging the hype train involving Manning. And now addressing how it’s hit brief shaky ground. “But he’s edgy right now,” Sarkisian said. “And honestly, I appreciate that about him. At some point, he’s gotta fight back. And the best way for him to fight back is going out and playing really good football with his teammates and enjoy playing football with his teammates. And so I’m looking forward to watching him compete Saturday night.” So Sarkisian is all in on Manning leading the slumping Longhorns against No. 7 Ole Miss. Even with Manning fading on NFL Draft boards and Texas facing a stunning third loss after briefly shooting up to No. 1. Related: New Maryland coach makes intriguing first move after replacing Mike Locksley Related: A Kamario Taylor return for Mississippi State-Oklahoma gaining more optimism

item.title: Make this chippy Alabama-Auburn basketball feud annual | Goodbread
item.description: BIRMINGHAM — It took less than five minutes of clock time for The Feud to be aptly named. Alabama basketball tangled with archrival Auburn in an exhibition game at Legacy Arena Thursday, Oct. 23, and won 87-84 − and it didn't take long for the tangling to go individual. With the Tigers leading 11-9 just before the first media timeout, Crimson Tide forward Keitenn Bristow and Auburn forward Thomas Dowd, all 430 combined pounds of them, hit the floor with a thud to battle for a rebound. Four hands wrestled for it, and after the whistle blew, none of the four came off the ball. Things got chippy. Other players gathered and tangled a bit themselves. UA coach Nate Oats stepped straight into the commotion and offered an earful to Auburn's Kevin Overton, the nearest official and Auburn coach Steven Pearl, who also joined the fray. In the aftermath, four technical fouls hit the scoresheet. No legit punches were thrown, but neither team was there for niceties. It was March Madness-level intensity, but in October. And a beautiful thing. A fairly evenly split crowd went berserk, of course, and it was no small gathering. Legacy Arena's lower bowl was packed, and the vast majority of its upper deck was full (capacity 17,654). They exploded with all the passion these teams will engender when they meet twice in the forthcoming regular season (at Alabama Jan. 30, at Auburn March 6). And they were treated to a closely-contested battle that never lacked for an edge. Back and forth they went, trading baskets with 12 lead changes, delivering some serious rivalry entertainment. HIGHLIGHTS: Auburn threatens Alabama basketball late in exhibition: Live updates, highlights THE FEUD: See Auburn basketball vs Alabama get chippy early in exhibition They used to bring their football teams to Birmingham for a game that was anything but an exhibition, back when Iron Bowls made Legion Field tremble once a year. And while there were good reasons for making Alabama-Auburn football a campus home-and-home series, there was nothing quite like the 50-50 crowd split, at 80,000-plus, that a neutral site created. It's been 28 years since the last Birmingham Iron Bowl, but here in 2026, exhibition basketball will still pack a house with orange- and crimson-clad yellers and screamers. Contrast that with the atmosphere in a standard exhibition game against a weaker opponent − UA drew a few thousand for a home showing against Furman two weeks ago − and it's a no-brainer to make this event annual. It makes too much sense, and judging by the size of the crowd, too much money. Most of all, the players – at least in this first-edition run – treated it like it meant something to them. They pushed and scrapped and dove on the floor. They played defense and threw elbows. And as Bristow and Dowd proved, they didn't mind getting testy, either. They feuded at The Feud. And there's no reason not to do it again in 12 months. Tuscaloosa News columnist Chase Goodbread is also the weekly co-host of Crimso

item.title: FCS Week 8 Game of the Week: North Dakota Hawks @ South Dakota Coyotes: How to Watch, Preview, Predictions
item.description: LINCOLN, NE - SEPTEMBER 19: North Dakota quarterback Jerry Kaminski (1) evades a tackle during the game between the North Dakota Fighting Hawks and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on September 19, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Date: Saturday, October 24 Time: 2:00 PM (ET) TV: ESPN+ The Quick Hits As it probably will for the rest of the regular season, the Missouri Valley has one of the premier matchups of the weekend in the FCS. This week #6 North Dakota, fresh of a huge home win over South Dakota State, squares off with the other team from the Mount Rushmore State. The Hawks take their 3-1 conference record on the road to Vermillion to take on South Dakota in a game that will have a whole awful lot to say about the playoff picture in about a month. The #8 Coyotes are in the midst of their own postseason push and share a similar 6-2 overall record with UND. South Dakota has won three straight but the level of competition is going to ramp up significantly on Saturday. Last year when these two came together it was the ‘Yotes who escaped with a 26-21 victory. Now, almost a year later in the same building, USD is looking to get the better of their neighbors to the North once more and if they do this time, it seems like they’ll be on the fast track to a top eight seed and, perhaps, a league title. The Coaches Eric Schmidt began running the ship for North Dakota last year and the transition from longtime head man Bubba Schweigert has been a relatively smooth one so far. In his first season, Schmidt led UND to the postseason and won a game before getting bounced in the second round to a very good Tarleton State squad. In year two he has the Hawks already two wins away from tying last year’s total and, if he pulls it off over South Dakota, it will be his ninth conference victory in a league that is extremely deep and talented. Schmidt is a North Dakota alum, having played linebacker for the Hawks (then Fighting Sioux) from 1998 to 2001. His counterpart on Saturday will be another guy who’s just getting his feet wet as a head coach. South Dakota’s Matt Vitzthum is in his inaugural season heading up the Coyotes after serving as the team’s wide receivers coach in 2024 then quarterbacks coach/co-offensive coordinator last fall. item.content:encoded: LINCOLN, NE - SEPTEMBER 19: North Dakota quarterback Jerry Kaminski (1) evades a tackle during the game between the North Dakota Fighting Hawks and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on September 19, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Date: Saturday, October 24 Time: 2:00 PM (ET) TV: ESPN+ The Quick Hits As it probably will for the rest of the regular season, the Missouri Valley has one of the premier matchups of the weekend in the FCS. This week #6 North Dakota, fresh of a huge home win over South Dakota State, squares off with the other team from the Mount Rushmore State. The Hawks take their 3-1 conference record on the road to Vermillion to take on South Dakota in a game that will have a whole awful lot to say about the playoff picture in about a month. The #8 Coyotes are in the midst of their own postseason push and share a similar 6-2 overall record with UND. South Dakota has won three straight but the level of competition is going to ramp up significantly on Saturday. Last year when these two came together it was the ‘Yotes who escaped with a 26-21 victory. Now, almost a year later in the same building, USD is looking to get the better of their neighbors to the North once more and if they do this time, it seems like they’ll be on the fast track to a top eight seed and, perhaps, a league title. The Coaches Eric Schmidt began running the ship for North Dakota last year and the transition from longtime head man Bubba Schweigert has been a relatively smooth one so far. In his first season, Schmidt led UND to the postseason and won a game before getting bounced in the second round to a very good Tarleton State squad. In year two he has the Hawks already two wins away from tying last year’s total and, if he pulls it off over South Dakota, it will be his ninth conference victory in a league that is extremely deep and talented. Schmidt is a North Dakota alum, having played linebacker for the Hawks (then Fighting Sioux) from 1998 to 2001. His counterpart on Saturday will be another guy who’s just getting his feet wet as a head coach. South Dakota’s Matt Vitzthum is in his inaugural season heading up the Coyotes after serving as the team’s wide receivers coach in 2024 then quarterbacks coach/co-offensive coordinator last fall. Vitzthum took over in short order for Travis Johansen who moved on after just one season. He has not missed a beat, though, and has the ‘Yotes playing at the high level they’ve become accustom to as of late. North Dakota Offense vs. South Dakota Defense The UND offense got a big boost last week with the return of senior quarterback Jerry Kaminski. Kaminski, who went down a couple weeks ago, came back and played well last week against SDSU after there was some worry he might miss time. The Hawks will need him in order to keep up in these big games they have coming down the pipe. He’s thrown for 1,742 yards and 21 touchdowns this year and is completing passes at a 66.8% clip thanks in large part to the some of the lethal receiving weapons he has at his disposal. Korey Tai and Deng Deng will be the two targets that Kaminski looks to the most. Deng leads the team with 518 receiving yards on 34 catches while Tai is the scoring leader with five TD grabs. The duo has been tough to stop for most every defense they’ve faced this year and the Coyotes are going to have a tall order, especially with some of their talented secondary pieces missing. R.J. Stewart has missed the last two games for USD and, if he can’t go in this one there’s a real chance that Kaminski along with his receivers could feast. Guys like Kael Kolarik and Ethan Carrier will need to step up because Deng and Kai will be some of the best wideouts they’ve seen up to this point. Both Carrier and Kolarik have one interception as well as 48 combined tackles this year. The Coyotes will also lean on one of the Missouri Valley’s best tacklers in senior linebacker Wade Abrams to shore up the middle. Abrams has 68 stops this year along with two forced fumbles. He is very active for the defense and will play a big role in not only spying Kaminski but also stopping running backs Charles Langama and Matt Lawson. The tandem of Langama and Lawson has been great for the Hawks. They have teamed up for 925 rush yards and nine touchdowns this year. Langama is averaging nearly eight yards per touch and has been nearly impossible to stop when he gets momentum going. South Dakota Offense vs. North Dakota Defense North Dakota got the win last week over SDSU because their defense stepped up and smothered a usually-effective quarterback in Chase Mason. This week the game plan has to be the exact same same against freshman phenom Austyn Modrzewski. Modrzewski won the starting job over the offseason and hasn’t looked back, tossing 22 touchdowns and averaging almost ten yards per attempt. He has delivered some exceptional performances, especially as of late. Over the last three games, Modrzewski has completed 49-of-70 attempts for 617 yards, seven touchdowns and just one pick. UND, though, has really come into its own, specifically in the secondary and last week may have been their finest performance yet in that department. Sophomore defensive back Grant Noland was one of the stars of the day against the Jackrabbits, posting six pass breakups on his own, bringing his season total up to 13. Noland led a unit that forced 20 incompletions and allowed just 169 passing yards last weekend. Again, they’ll need to use that as the blueprint because if they can’t slow down Modrzewski, it’s going to be a long day. No doubt the biggest bolster to the defense, though, has been the return of star pass rusher Lance Rucker. Rucker missed the first half of the season with an ankle injury he suffered right before the first game. He came back against South Dakota State and his impact was immediately felt. He registered three QB hurries and the unit as a whole was able to play so much more freely with him wreaking havoc up front. Rucker will be a massive part of trying to make Modrzewski uncomfortable in the pocket. The Coyotes will need to relieve some pressure off of their young quarterback and, in order to do that, they’ll need running back Charles Pierre Jr. Last week he did not play mostly out of caution as he did not feel 100% in warmups. Without him, though, the USD offense is not as dynamic. He’s ran for 604 yards and seven touchdowns on 90 carries. For those doing the math, that’s good for an average of 6.5 yards per carry. If he’s back, and it sounds like Vitzthum is optimistic he will be, then the ‘Yotes will be much more equip to deal with what UND will throw at them. South Dakota will also need to continue to get production from their receiving corps. Brayden White and Tennel Bryant are the primary pass catchers. Each has over 400 yards and, between the two of them, have 11 scores this season. Prediction This game is extremely difficult to get a real read on because it depends almost entirely on what teams shows up on either side. Will it be the North Dakota squad that lost to Northern Iowa or the one that looked like a national championship contender last week? Will the South Dakota squad that looked lost against YSU be there on Saturday or will it be the one that has allowed just 14.7 points per contest over the last three weeks? Both teams are very well-built but both have had a rocky recent history in these sorts of massive games. Homefield advantage has been big for the Coyotes this year as they haven’t lost a game in the DakotaDome yet this year. Modrzewski is a frontrunner for the Jerry Rice Award and he will show why even with Rucker on the other side. In a close game, he’ll make the game-winning throw late to get it done. Score Prediction: South Dakota: 27 – North Dakota 23

item.title: Wright State vs. Air Force Stars, Stripes and Flight Classic tickets sell out
item.description: Wright State University Tickets are sold out for the Stars, Stripes and Flight Classic men’s basketball game between the Wright State Raiders and the Air Force Falcons on Nov. 2 at the Nutter Center in Dayton. [DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] The game serves as the home opener for Wright State while honoring Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, the U.S. Air Force, veterans and active-duty military. The matchup opens the season for Wright State, the defending Horizon League champion. The Raiders have reached the NCAA Tournament in two of the past five seasons. TRENDING STORIES: Todd Benzinger, World Series champ with Reds, dies at 63 Gov. Mike DeWine denounces Ramaswamy ad featuring Dr. Amy Acton’s estranged mother Coroner IDs 14-year-old killed in Dayton hit-and-run crash The game also kicks off local initiatives for The Big Hoopla as the region prepares for the return of the NCAA First Four to Dayton in March 2027. Wright State Athletic Director Brad Chandler commented on the ticket sales for the season opener. “Fans have stepped up for both the Raiders and Falcons in an unprecedented show of support,” Chandler said. “We’ve hinted at a few surprises, but simply put, the Nutter Center will be the place to be for the opening night of college basketball.” Ticket holders will receive a free Vintage Rowdy T-shirt at the venue entrance before the 7 p.m. tipoff.

item.description: 🏈 Find Thursday night football coverage here ⚽ BOYS SOCCER - Division I Smithfield 2, Classical 0 The Sentinels will enter the Division II boys soccer playoffs on a 10-match unbeaten run and as the top seed after blanking the Purple, 2-0, on a gorgeous fall Thursday night at Morro Athletic Complex. Noah Albaret and Sebastian Santos each found the net early in the second half as Smithfield dealt Classical just its second league defeat of the season. The Sentinels are all but certain to remain in front of Scituate in the RPI standings and will receive a bye into next week's quarterfinals. Smithfield found the breakthrough it needed through Albaret in the 46th minute. Steven Coutcher knocked one down in front and Albaret was waiting, pulling his shot inside the left post. That gave the Sentinels a 1-0 edge and some momentum. Smithfield (14-2-1) doubled the lead with some insurance in the 54th minute after serving in a free kick off the right side. Senai Zerit made a couple fine saves from close range, but Santos finally stuck away a rebound off an Ethan Cataldo shot to make it 2-0. The Purple (8-2-6) were under pressure early but came inches from opening the scoring late in the first half when a Marc Lombardi-Ortiz header caromed off the right post and away. Classical saw another chance turned aside when J akob Johnson parried a 20-yard shot from Lombardi-Ortiz comfortably over the crossbar. That was the last of the real chances for the Purple, who entered the night at the No. 3 seed and could still avoid an uncomfortable preliminary match this weekend. This result ended their own 10-match unbeaten run, a stretch dating back to a 4-1 loss against Central Falls on Sept. 15. ⚽ Other Boys Soccer scores : Narragansett 6, Prout 1 Ponaganset 3, Middletown 0 Hendricken 4, Lincoln 3 Portsmouth 8, North Smithfield 1 East Greenwich 2, Cumberland 0 ⚽ GIRLS SOCCER - Division I Chariho 2, East Providence 0 Chariho scored twice in the first half and relied on a strong defensive effort to earn a 2-0 victory over East Providence. Eiley Simmons put Chariho ahead just three minutes into the game, winning the ball outside the 18-yard box before firing a shot past the goalkeeper for a 1-0 lead. With 10 minutes remaining in the first half, Finley Campbell set up Dylan Whitman , who drove past a defender and finished to double the advantage. Chariho controlled possession for much of the game, but East Providence packed its defense and made it difficult for the Chargers to find open passing lanes and generate quality chances. Savana Debont-Fitzgerald preserved the shutout with four saves in goal for Chariho. East Providence's goalkeeper turned aside six shots. Moses Brown 1, Smithfield 0 Avery Butler provided the game’s only goal for the Quakers, converting a penalty kick with Rose Couto credited with the assist. Moses Brown goalkeeper Marielle Nassiff made the lead stand with nine saves to earn the shutout. Smithfield goalie Gabby Buco kept the Sentinels within striking

item.title: Devils Steamroll Ducks Early, Never Cough Up Lead With Strong Defense in 4-1 Win
item.description: NEWARK, NJ - OCTOBER 22: Anthony Mantha #39 of the New Jersey Devils celebrates after scoring during the third period of the game against the Anaheim Ducks on October 22, 2026 at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images First Period The match between the New Jersey Devils and the Anaheim Ducks started a bit slowly, as the top two lines came and went without a shot. The third line did their best to play some back-and-forth hockey, but a long shot in off an offensive zone hold from Evan Rodrigues was stopped. Declan Chisholm crashed for the rebound, which bounced over his stick and forced Dawson Mercer to jump back next to Johnny Kovacevic against the rush as Nico Daws gloved at but didn’t hold a long shot from Nikita Klepov (this shot was taken off the board because it was set to go wide into crashing traffic, as bettors have really gotten ahold of shot counts in the NHL). With those slow opening shifts, Anaheim made an early mistake in not bringing the energy to the Devils. With Jack Hughes posted up at the center of the blueline in the offensive zone, he was largely unpressured as Anaheim struggled to block passing lanes following good puck movement around the top of the zone. Jack fed Jesper Bratt in the lower edge of the faceoff circle, and Bratt turned it inside to Arseny Gritsyuk for an easy tap-in goal as the Devils took the early lead! Luke Hughes had a great defensive period, breaking up two odd-man rushes by being aggressive against the puck carrier on both occasions. The Devils were doing well as a whole, blocking shots and not actually allowing an official shot on goal until they were 14 and a half minutes into the game, as Nico Daws padded a point shot away. Just as the Devils looked like they had given away the puck right to the front of the net with two minutes to play, Alex Killorn was sent to the box for tripping Johnny Kovacevic. The whistle blew as Roger McQueen shot on Daws, negating it, but the trip was so obvious that it wasn’t even contested by the Ducks. Still, as the replay showed, Kovacevic made the giveaway without Killorn’s help, passing from his backhand right to McQueen before being taken down. Evangelista took a one-timer from beyond the high slot that went right into Nico Hischier’s chest, and it seemed to sting a bit as the Devils kept possession. item.content:encoded: NEWARK, NJ - OCTOBER 22: Anthony Mantha #39 of the New Jersey Devils celebrates after scoring during the third period of the game against the Anaheim Ducks on October 22, 2026 at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images First Period The match between the New Jersey Devils and the Anaheim Ducks started a bit slowly, as the top two lines came and went without a shot. The third line did their best to play some back-and-forth hockey, but a long shot in off an offensive zone hold from Evan Rodrigues was stopped. Declan Chisholm crashed for the rebound, which bounced over his stick and forced Dawson Mercer to jump back next to Johnny Kovacevic against the rush as Nico Daws gloved at but didn’t hold a long shot from Nikita Klepov (this shot was taken off the board because it was set to go wide into crashing traffic, as bettors have really gotten ahold of shot counts in the NHL). With those slow opening shifts, Anaheim made an early mistake in not bringing the energy to the Devils. With Jack Hughes posted up at the center of the blueline in the offensive zone, he was largely unpressured as Anaheim struggled to block passing lanes following good puck movement around the top of the zone. Jack fed Jesper Bratt in the lower edge of the faceoff circle, and Bratt turned it inside to Arseny Gritsyuk for an easy tap-in goal as the Devils took the early lead! Luke Hughes had a great defensive period, breaking up two odd-man rushes by being aggressive against the puck carrier on both occasions. The Devils were doing well as a whole, blocking shots and not actually allowing an official shot on goal until they were 14 and a half minutes into the game, as Nico Daws padded a point shot away. Just as the Devils looked like they had given away the puck right to the front of the net with two minutes to play, Alex Killorn was sent to the box for tripping Johnny Kovacevic. The whistle blew as Roger McQueen shot on Daws, negating it, but the trip was so obvious that it wasn’t even contested by the Ducks. Still, as the replay showed, Kovacevic made the giveaway without Killorn’s help, passing from his backhand right to McQueen before being taken down. The Devils’ power play started off slowly, but it got going in the second minute. The Ducks had the puck in the Devils’ offensive zone, but Luke Hughes took it away and tried to spring them on a rush chance. They were a little disjointed, passing back to Luke Evangelista who was trailing in, and the five Devils each stood on the perimeter of the offensive zone for a few moments to establish possession before getting into their usual set-up. Evangelista took a one-timer from beyond the high slot that went right into Nico Hischier’s chest, and it seemed to sting a bit as the Devils kept possession. Hischier would be rewarded for playing through it when Jack Hughes shot on goal from the lower right faceoff circle, giving Nico a perfect rebound to tap into the goal! The Devils took this 2-0 lead into the intermission. Second Period Early in the second period, Brett Pesce took an uncalled high stick from AJ Greer behind the Devils’ net. Pesce got into it with the Ducks in the corner afterwards and then crosschecked Greer in front of the Devils’ net, giving Anaheim their first power play of the game. The Devils’ penalty kill did very well, only allowing one shot on goal while clearing the puck several times. The Devils would later be called for another penalty when Evan Rodrigues went to the box for a four-minute high sticking double minor at nine and a half minutes into the period. After review, the penalty was wiped off the board as it was called a follow-through of Rodrigues playing the puck along the wall. Throughout the following minutes, Nico Daws got a lot more action in goal, getting across the 10-save mark, including one point shot that was deflected down to the ice and gloved when it bounced back above his pad. Third Period After a slow start to the final frame, the Ducks pulled within one eight and a half minutes into the period when a Jackson LaCombe point shot was tipped past Nico Daws by Tim Washe. All the sudden the Devils, who went into coast mode a bit too early, were one bad shot against away from being stunned into a tie game. As the period progressed, the Devils were slow to create scoring chances, but it would be Anthony Mantha who gave them their crucial goal. Mantha was screening Ville Husso uncovered, swinging at a Brett Pesce point shot and digging away at Husso before he was able to freeze the puck. It went through the five hole, and the Devils extended their lead to 3-1 with over six and a half minutes to play. The Ducks pulled Husso with over four and a half minutes to play, trying to pull back to within one. But the undisciplined Ducks would take a penalty in the corner. As Alex Killorn was doing his best to take a crosschecking penalty on Nico Hischier, Bennett Sennecke took a high sticking penalty on Luke Evangelista as the teams battled for the puck. This put Ville Husso back in the net as the Devils sent out Luke Hughes and Dougie Hamilton for a two-defenseman power play. Hamilton just missed a chip shot wide early on, and Jesper Bratt just missed his stick with a pass from behind the net. Sheldon Keefe rewarded other players with some power play shifts after the first unit went off for a stoppage, and Connor Brown came very close on two chances but was stymied by Husso. With Husso out of the net in the final half minute, Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt checked relentlessly to prevent the Ducks from crossing center ice as they hunted for that empty net goal. It was Jack who finally got it done, one-handing the puck away at the blueline and smoothly backhanding it into the net to seal the game at 4-1. The Game Stats: The NHL.com Game Summary | The NHL.com Event Summary | The NHL.com Play by Play Log | The NHL.com Shot Summary | The Natural Stat Trick Game Stats | The Post Hockey Game Stats | Hockey Game Bot The Devils Are Back It might not have been pretty to start the season, but the New Jersey Devils seem to be back from an offensive standpoint. With this game, the Devils have: Outshot opponents in 10 of 10 games Out-xG’d opponents in 8 of 10 games Scored first in their last five games Won four of their last five There is still a lot of season to go, but it seems that when the Devils set the tone with their game, it is really hard for opponents to claw it back from them. Even in the second period, the Devils only allowed eight shots while out-chancing the Ducks. What has been a bit different over these last two wins is that it has just about entirely been the Hischier and Hughes lines leading the way. Those two lines accounted for a 14-6 shots advantage at five-on-five, while the bottom six was outshot 8-5. But the bottom six isn’t all bad. They need to figure out their even strength configuration, but Connor Brown has been a boost on the penalty kill already and almost made the most of his half-shift of power play ice time. Anthony Mantha, in an intermedial shift with Nico Hischier and Dawson Mercer, scored his second goal of the year to give the Devils a cushion at the end of the game. I do think the Devils look better at five-on-five when Amadeus Lombardi is driving offense on the fourth line, but it’s going to have to be a tough call for Sheldon Keefe to see who has to come out of the lineup for him to do that. Luke Hughes and Dougie Hamilton Their on-ice stats might not be the best today because of the Ducks’ second period shootaround, but today was a great defensive showing for Luke Hughes and Dougie Hamilton. If not for Luke, the Ducks would have had multiple odd-man rushes in the first period, and Luke was great at peeling away from Ducks with the puck today. More and more, it looks like it’s all coming together for him, even though he has been very unlucky in terms of appearing on the scoresheet when he isn’

item.title: ‘They Are Very Unhappy’ — Super Bowl Champion Urges Giants To Make Trade for $44M All-Pro To Solve Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. Dilemma
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Week 6 saw the New York Giants fall to the New Orleans Saints, but there was a silver lining: J.J. McCarthy’s debut. One man Giants fans did not see on the field, though, was running back Cam Skattebo. Skattebo, the team’s leading rusher this season, was healthy and active for the game, but did not get a carry against New Orleans. McCarthy, who entered the game midway through, finished as the team’s leading rusher. There’s been more than enough speculation since then over how the Giants will handle their RB room, and one former offensive lineman believes there is a perfect solution on the trade market. Giants Urged To Swing Jonathan Taylor Trade Super Bowl champion Andrew Whitworth was working Amazon Prime’s coverage of Thursday Night Football. Before the Week 7 clash between the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears, Whitworth suggested the Giants go for broke to fix their running back situation. “If you look across the league, with Chris Ballard being fired as the GM in Indianapolis, there should be an arms race around the league for some of the veteran talent there. You got a lot of guys entering the final years of their contracts, some talented football players,” Whitworth began . “The New York Giants, that’s the one I have circled. In the NFC, you think of that running back situation they’re very unhappy with. What has John Harbaugh done since he came from Baltimore? He’s brought a whole lot of Baltimore influence into that team… Could he go get his Derrick Henry? Bring Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants,” Whitworth continued. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator "Bring Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants." @AndrewWhitworth has a trade idea for the Giants 👀 #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/C6vFc1XgEl — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) The Giants could be in a position to make a splash. New York sits atop the NFC East at 3-2-1. The Washington Commanders are 1-4-1, while the Philadelphia Eagles have lost quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season. The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4, but could still challenge New York for the division. Taylor would certainly make a ton of sense as a trade candidate. As Whitworth pointed out, the Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after Week 6. In 10 seasons, Ballard’s Colts played just three playoff games. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer This has created the potential for a fire sale at the upcoming NFL Trade Deadline. If the Colts are open for business, Taylor could be one of the most in-demand players on the market. This season, Taylor has scored seven touchdowns while racking up 655 yards from scrimmage. His 80.6 PFN RB Impact Grade ranks #10 in the league. Taylor’s contract is part of the reason he could be on the move. He signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August, keeping him under contract through 2028. However, ESPN’s Dan Graziano has noted that the deal does not necessarily prevent Indianapolis from trading hi

He’s brought a whole lot of Baltimore influence into that team… Could he go get his Derrick Henry? Bring Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants,” Whitworth continued. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator "Bring Jonathan Taylor to the New York Giants." @AndrewWhitworth has a trade idea for the Giants 👀 #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/C6vFc1XgEl — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) The Giants could be in a position to make a splash. New York sits atop the NFC East at 3-2-1. The Washington Commanders are 1-4-1, while the Philadelphia Eagles have lost quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season. The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4, but could still challenge New York for the division. Taylor would certainly make a ton of sense as a trade candidate. As Whitworth pointed out, the Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after Week 6. In 10 seasons, Ballard’s Colts played just three playoff games. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer This has created the potential for a fire sale at the upcoming NFL Trade Deadline. If the Colts are open for business, Taylor could be one of the most in-demand players on the market. This season, Taylor has scored seven touchdowns while racking up 655 yards from scrimmage. His 80.6 PFN RB Impact Grade ranks #10 in the league. Taylor’s contract is part of the reason he could be on the move. He signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August, keeping him under contract through 2028. However, ESPN’s Dan Graziano has noted that the deal does not necessarily prevent Indianapolis from trading him. What the Colts do with their talent certainly remains to be seen. In any event, the Giants make sense as a potential landing spot. If they can find an agreeable deal, Taylor would be a massive upgrade for New York. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Cavaliers score tonight vs. 76ers. Cavs blow big lead, again, lose
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points as the Philadelphia 76ers erased a 29-point deficit in a wild 114-106 victory over the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday, Oct. 22. Joel Embiid added 24 points for Philadelphia, which dominated the second half for the second consecutive game after opening the season Tuesday with a road victory over the New York Knicks . This rally was even more emphatic, as the Sixers outscored the Cavaliers 69-37 after halftime. Playing in front of the home crowd for the first time as 76ers, LeBron James scored 17 points and grabbed 10 rebounds, while Jaylen Brown scored 10 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter. Cleveland fell short in its season opener despite Donovan Mitchell 's 32 points and 10 rebounds. Evan Mobley added 18 points for the Cavaliers, while James Harden had 16 and Jarrett Allen notched 14. After trailing by 24 at halftime, Philadelphia needed only 78 seconds to cut the deficit to 13, as James found Embiid for a layup to make it 69-56. Maxey's layup with 5:42 left in the third quarter brought the Sixers back within 10. Philadelphia got as close as 84-82 before Mario Hezonja made two late bank shots, helping the Cavaliers carry a 90-82 lead into the fourth. Embiid's running floater with 7:20 left drew the Sixers within 95-94. He knocked down a 15-footer on the next trip to give the team its first lead of the night. Brown scored the next six points and Maxey added a bucket to cap a 15-0 push, giving the Sixers a 104-95 lead. Cleveland got within 106-102 down the stretch, but Mitchell missed two free throws, and the momentum was squashed. Maxey and Brown scored on the next two trips to push the lead back to eight. The Cavaliers stormed out of the gates, taking a 35-18 lead after 12 lopsided minutes. The Sixers shot 38.1% in the first quarter and committed eight turnovers. They committed six more turnovers in the second quarter en route to a 69-45 deficit at intermission. Mobley scored 11 second-quarter points and Mitchell had 10 for Cleveland, which led by as many as 29 points in the period. Mitchell paced all scorers with 22 points at the break. The Akron Beacon Journal sports department can be contacted via email at bjsports@thebeaconjournal.com. This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: Cavaliers score tonight vs. 76ers. Cavs blow big lead, again, lose

item.title: 'I feel horrible:' LASA forfeits the 3 games left on its high school football schedule
item.description: Players listen to instructions from coaches during football practice at Liberal Arts and Science Academy Thursday, Sept. 21, 2023. LASA football is 4-0 for the first time in school history. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) LASA's football season is over. The Liberal Arts and Science Academy will forfeit its three remaining District 12-5A Division II games against Pflugerville, Crockett and Bastrop due to low numbers, Austin school district athletic director Jason Glenn confirmed Thursday night. "It's unfortunate," Glenn told the American-Statesman. "We're working through some things to make sure that those kids have a good and safe experience the rest of the way." Pflugerville ISD athletics posted on social media Thursday afternoon that LASA, which was 0-7 entering this week, had forfeited Friday's game against Pflugerville. But Glenn said the Raptors' season is done and he has contacted Bastrop ISD officials regarding the Nov. 5 game against the Bears. (Crockett is an Austin ISD school already overseen by Glenn.) Glenn noted he sympathizes with the three other schools affected. "I feel horrible, not just for the Austin ISD kids, but for those kids from other districts who worked all offseason and all summer," he said. "And not just the football players, but the band, fine arts and cheer kids. Schools deserve to have 10 football games." Friday's game at the Pfield was supposed to be Pflugerville's homecoming, but that has now been rescheduled for Nov. 5 against Crockett. LASA only scored 26 points this season and has been shut out four times. It's the second time in three years that LASA, which has struggled with participation, has affected other area schools' schedules. Two weeks after the UIL released its biennial realignment in February 2024, LASA informed its district opponents it would not be playing a UIL varsity schedule for that district cycle, forcing the district football schedule to be redrawn. That left several Central Texas schools, including Pflugerville, Crockett and Bastrop, scrambling to find another opponent at a time when most programs had already solidified their schedules. LASA Principal Stacia Crescenzi cited safety concerns and numbers for that decision. The Raptors played a non-honors schedule in both 2024 and 2025, competing mainly against private schools. High school sports reporter Shaun Chornobroff contributed to this report. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. This article originally published at 'I feel horrible:' LASA forfeits the 3 games left on its high school football schedule .

item.title: Collin Sexton cleared for Lakers debut amid calf injury, Jake LaRavia questionable
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Collin Sexton cleared for Lakers debut amid calf injury, Jake LaRavia questionable appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Veteran guard Collin Sexton was cleared to make his Los Angeles Lakers debut on Friday against the LA Clippers as he was no longer listed on the team’s injury report. Sexton had been sidelined for all preseason and had only recently begun fully participating in practice amid a calf injury. Collin Sexton was initially listed as questionable on the Lakers’ injury report for their season opener against the Golden State Warriors, but was eventually ruled out. Without the nine-year veteran in the lineup, Lakers head coach JJ Redick opted to bring Quentin Grimes off the bench. That was a move that was first done during the final preseason game in an effort to provide the second unit with an experienced ball-handler and cut down on turnovers. As far as the rest of the Lakers’ injury report is concerned, forward Jake LaRavia is listed as questionable due to a right ankle sprain he sustained against the Warriors. The moment happened about midway through the fourth quarter when he came off a screen, attacked the basket and fell to the ground before getting to the rim. He stayed down for a while under the Lakers’ basket before being helped up. He was able to walk off to the locker room under his own power. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) To that point, LaRavia had seemingly regained his form and confidence from last season. He ended the game with 10 points, two rebounds, two assists and one steal while shooting 4-of-5 from the field and 2-of-3 from the 3-point line in 18 minutes. Sexton, on the other hand, comes in after splitting last season between the Charlotte Hornets and Chicago Bulls. He was one of the Lakers’ initial free agent signings during their early splurge that included Grimes, Walker Kessler and Sandro Mamukelashvili. The No. 8 overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft, he appeared in a total of 68 games, including 22 starts, at a little over 23 minutes per game. He averaged 15.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 48.5 percent shooting from the field, 40.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 85.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Related: JJ Redick reveals hilarious reason for Luka Doncic’s half-court shot efficiency Related: Luka Doncic’s ex-Mavericks teammate warns Yaxel Lendeborg about his comments — ‘80 ball next time’

item.title: Karl-Heinz Rummenigge would love to see Harry Kane bring the Ballon d’Or back to Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) (Photo by FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich honorary president Karl-Heinz Rummenigge would love to see Harry Kane become the next player from the club to win the Ballon d’Or, believing the English striker has a compelling case thanks to his individual performances and trophy haul. Rummenigge knows what it takes to reach the summit of the sport, having won the prestigious individual award in 1980. More than four decades later, he hopes Kane can follow in his footsteps and deliver another historic moment for the German giants. “I was the last Bayern player to win the award, so I would like to see another Bayern player win it now. That would have a very special significance for us as a club as well. The decisive criterion is individual performance, and Harry Kane has the edge there – his goals and his trophies speak for themselves,” Rummenigge told ranSport (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Kane has established himself as one of Europe’s most prolific forwards since joining Bayern Munich, combining extraordinary goalscoring numbers with his ability to influence matches at the highest level. His continued success in Munich has strengthened his credentials among the world’s elite players. Of course, winning major trophies will remain crucial to his chances. If Kane continues delivering individually while leading Bayern Munich to silverware, could he finally become the club’s next Ballon d’Or winner? Join the conversation! His continued success in Munich has strengthened his credentials among the world’s elite players. Of course, winning major trophies will remain crucial to his chances. If Kane continues delivering individually while leading Bayern Munich to silverware, could he finally become the club’s next Ballon d’Or winner? Join the conversation! item.title: Maple Leafs’ William Nylander has hilarious question about Brady Tkachuk’s Ottawa return
item.description: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Maple Leafs’ William Nylander has hilarious question about Brady Tkachuk’s Ottawa return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Wednesday evening, the highly anticipated return of former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk to Canadian Tire Centre took place. And while Tkachuk scored the first goal of the game, the Senators responded with several unanswered goals of their own en route to a 4-1 victory. The game was marked by multiple anti-Tkachuk chants from the crowd, including multiple profanity-laced chants, as plenty of Ottawa fans felt a sense of betrayal from the former captain who had affirmed his commitment to the team following their loss in the Stanley Cup Playoffs earlier in the spring. Watching from afar, Toronto Maple Leafs forward William Nylander , who knows all about the kind of vitriol that fans of a rival fan base can bring, had a hilarious question about the former Senators’ captain’s return to his old venue. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Were they throwing snakes at Brady?” Nylander asked via TSN on X, formerly known as Twitter. Nylander well remembers the return of current Maple Leafs teammate John Tavares to the Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum in 2019 after he bolted from the New York Islanders to sign with his hometown club, facing a highly hostile crowd that serenaded the veteran forward with vulgar chants throughout the game; there were even a few plastic snakes that were thrown onto the ice in his direction by angry fans. Tkachuk requested to be traded from the Senators not long after their opening-round playoff loss to the eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, and he was dealt to the divisional rival Florida Panthers, who already featured his brother Matthew Tkachuk. Related: Auston Matthews joins exclusive Maple Leafs club during Blue Jackets clash
