item.title: 76ers rally to stun Cavs in James's first home game for Philadelphia
item.description: Philadelphia's LeBron James puts up a basket over Evan Mobley in the 76ers' first home game of the NBA season against the Cleveland Cavaliers (Emilee Chinn) The Philadelphia 76ers erased a 29-point deficit to stun the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Thursday in NBA superstar LeBron James's first home game since landing in Philly as a free agent. Tyrese Maxey scored 32 points and Joel Embiid added 24 -- including a jump shot with 6:54 left to play that gave the Sixers their first lead of the night, one they wouldn't relinquish. Former Celtics star Jaylen Brown, the Sixers' other big off-season acquisition, scored 21 points and pulled down eight rebounds and four-time NBA champion James added 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists to help the 76ers author their biggest comeback of the play-by-play era that started in 1996. Cleveland, disappointed not to land hometown hero James after he announced he was leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons, appeared to be on a mission to show him what he missed. James won one of his four championships with Cleveland, and Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson admitted before the game that James's decision to pursue a fifth crown with the 76ers left him "just depressed, honestly" for the first couple of days after the move was announced. But he had reason to be pleased with the Cavaliers' start to their first game of the new season. Donovan Mitchell scored 22 of his 32 points in the first half as the Cavs seized control against a 76ers team struggling to find a rhythm and protect the ball. Philadelphia center Joel Embiid looked creaky, and James had five of the Sixers' 15 first-half turnovers -- which led to 22 Cavs points and provoked boos from Philly fans whose hopes of a title run have been raised by the arrivals of James and Brown. The boos turned to raucous cheers as the re-energized 76ers opened the third quarter on an 11-0 run. They cut the lead to single digits on back-to-back baskets from Maxey that pulled them within 80-73. The Cavs were struggling to regroup. Maxey reduced the deficit to two points with a running finger roll layup with 2:33 left in the third before Cleveland reeled off six straight points to take a 90-82 lead into the fourth quarter. But the 76ers kept coming. They out-scored the Cavaliers 60-37 in the second half, clamping down defensively and giving up just two turnovers. Evan Mobley scored 18 points for Cleveland but had just three in the second half Jarrett Allen scored 14 but was held scoreless after the break. bb/rcw

item.title: No. 1 Maryland field hockey’s unbeaten streak ends in 4-2 defeat against No. 2 Northwestern
item.description: For three quarters Thursday night in Evanston, Illinois, it was all No. 1 Maryland field hockey. For the final period, it was all Olivia Bent-Cole. The Northwestern senior registered a pair of fourth-quarter goals to complete both a hat trick and the No. 2 Wildcats’ comeback to stun the top-ranked Terps, 4-2. The loss snapped Maryland’s 14-game unbeaten streak. For a while, the first quarter was evenly-matched, as neither team claimed the upper hand. A mere one shot had been taken through the first 10 minutes. Eventually, both offenses woke up. On Maryland’s first set piece of the match, it drew first blood. Francisca Eschoyez’s drag flick from the top of the circle caught the stick of freshman Ella Beach, who ricocheted the shot past Northwestern goalkeeper Juliana Boon. In her homecoming game, the Northbrook, Illinois, native gave Maryland the lead eleven minutes in. It wouldn’t take long for Northwestern to respond. Despite failing on their first set piece, the Wildcats stayed persistent and found the back of the net. Bent-Cole collected a bouncing ball on the right wing and snapped a shot past Alyssa Klebasko to knot the score at one with less than a minute to play in the opening quarter. The second quarter nearly mirrored the first, as through 13 minutes, a single shot had been registered. Yet again, that changed with Maryland’s only penalty corner of the period. This time, Jordyn Hollamon did the honors, whacking a rocket to the back of the cage to put the Terps back up by a goal. It was the sophomore’s seventh tally of the season but just her second on a penalty corner. That gave Maryland a 2-1 halftime lead. The third quarter had similar tension, but this time, neither side cracked the code. Maryland had a trio of set pieces in the frame but Northwestern learned from its mistakes and held the Terps off the scoreboard. Immediately after the flurry of corners, Babs van Hest was whistled for a yellow card, rejuvenating the home side. The penalty corner department was a major area of focus for both sides entering Thursday night’s showdown. Prior to the game, Northwestern averaged an otherworldly 9.13 corners per game, by far the most in the Big Ten. The Terps turned the tables on Thursday, topping the Wildcats by three in corner attempts. Eventually, the Terps paid the price with the yellow card. Bent-Cole’s second finish of the night was the first of a three-goal onslaught in the fourth quarter – the last of which came via a redirection from Ella Kokinis. Northwestern was a changed team in the fourth quarter. Within the opening 6:30, the Wildcats had six shots, tripling the amount they had when the period started. By the end of the frame, the Wildcats had outshot the Terps, 8-2. Remarkably, they did that with minimal production from Ashley Sessa and Ilse Tromp, their two top offensive contributors coming into the match. The road doesn’t get any easier for the Terps. No. 13 Indiana awaits in Bloomington on Sunday. Three things to know: 1. Qua

The third quarter had similar tension, but this time, neither side cracked the code. Maryland had a trio of set pieces in the frame but Northwestern learned from its mistakes and held the Terps off the scoreboard. Immediately after the flurry of corners, Babs van Hest was whistled for a yellow card, rejuvenating the home side. Remarkably, they did that with minimal production from Ashley Sessa and Ilse Tromp, their two top offensive contributors coming into the match. The road doesn’t get any easier for the Terps. No. 13 Indiana awaits in Bloomington on Sunday. Three things to know: 1. Quality over quantity, this time for the opposition. Maryland held Northwestern to 10 shots, its second-lowest total of the season. Unfortunately for the Terps, the Wildcats converted on four of those 10 shots. 2. Challenged the Wildcats. Maryland joined Duke and Princeton as the only three squads to score multiple goals against Northwestern. But the Big Ten’s second-best offense was held to just nine shots, nearly tying its season-low. Boon registered just one stop Thursday. 3. Tournament check-in. Maryland now finds itself second in the Big Ten standings with two games to play before the conference tournament. For the Terps to earn the top seed and a bye to the semifinals, they’d have to win out and Northwestern would have to lose out – a relatively unlikely scenario considering the Wildcats’ dominance. For now, the Terps have their sights set on the No. 2 seed and a likely matchup with Michigan or Ohio State if they can clinch that second spot.

item.title: Rangers’ road woes continue as Maple Leafs win 5-4 on last-minute goal
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Rangers found another way to lose on the road. Their winless streak away from Madison Square Garden reached five games (0-4-1) when defenseman Troy Stetcher scored with 27.5 seconds remaining to give the Toronto Maple Leafs a 5-4 victory at Scotiabank Arena on Thursday night. Alexis Lafreniere’s goal with 5:35 remaining in the third period lifted the Rangers into a 4-4 tie. But Toronto controlled the play in the final minute, and with a delayed penalty call against New York’s Tye Kartye in effect, the Leafs lifted goalie Sergei Bobrovsky for an extra attacker. Stetcher raced into the right circle and ripped a shot that appeared to hit a Ranger and deflect upward past goaltender Dylan Garand. It was Stetcher’s first goal in 33 games and lifted the Maple Leafs to their third straight win. WHAT A SHOT, LAF 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/KjKleaBHGP — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 23, 2026 Toronto got a career-best three-point night (one goal, two assists) from fourth-liner Brandon Duhaime. Easton Cowan, Teddy Blueger and Kirill Marchenko also scored for Toronto, which outshot the Rangers 36-25. Bobrovsky made 21 saves for his 459th NHL win — tying Rangers Hall of Famer Henrik Lundqvist for sixth all-time. Adam Fox capped a four-assist night by setting up Lafreniere’s tying goal. Mika Zibanejad, Oliver Bjorkstrand and Kartye had the other goals for the Rangers. Garand finished with 31 saves and was the biggest reason the Blueshirts had a chance to get at least a point. The Rangers are 6-0-0 at home but haven’t won away from Madison Square Garden since defeating the Detroit Red Wings 2-0 on Oct. 2. They finish their two-game tour of Ontario with a visit to the Ottawa Senators on Saturday night. Rangers’ road struggles continue as Leafs score late for 5-4 win Toronto took advantage of a sloppy change on defense to grab the lead just 1:36 after the opening face-off. Jake McCabe found Cowan just as the second-year forward hit the blue line; he split the defense pair of Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson before beating Garand with a perfect wrist shot high past the goalie’s glove for a 1-0 lead. It was Toronto’s first shot of the game. The Rangers held the Leafs shotless for the next 5:15, and by that time the score was tied 1-1. The Blueshirts got even at 5:39 when Zibanejad set up in the slot and got a tip on Vladislav Gavrikov’s shot from the left point, deflecting it past Bobrovsky for his third of the season and first at even strength. Gavi with the shot + Mika deflects it in 👏 pic.twitter.com/1UoHJR4Uab — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 22, 2026 But the Rangers’ defense sprung another leak midway through the period, and Toronto again took advantage. The Leafs’ fourth line, which hadn’t produced a goal all season, struck at 10:01 when Blueger was left all alone in front of Garand. They finish their two-game tour of Ontario with a visit to the Ottawa Senators on Saturday night. Rangers’ road struggles continue as Leafs score late for 5-4 win Toronto took advantage of a sloppy change on defense to grab the lead just 1:36 after the opening face-off. The Blueshirts got even at 5:39 when Zibanejad set up in the slot and got a tip on Vladislav Gavrikov’s shot from the left point, deflecting it past Bobrovsky for his third of the season and first at even strength. Gavi with the shot + Mika deflects it in 👏 pic.twitter.com/1UoHJR4Uab — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 22, 2026 But the Rangers’ defense sprung another leak midway through the period, and Toronto again took advantage. The Leafs’ fourth line, which hadn’t produced a goal all season, struck at 10:01 when Blueger was left all alone in front of Garand. Duhaime slid the puck to him, and Blueger beat Garand through the pads to make it 2-1. The Rangers had the better of territorial play for the rest of the period, but only a couple of 10-bell saves by Garand kept the deficit to one goal. The rookie goaltender stopped Duhaime, who had raced down right wing untouched and cut to the net, then used his glove to foil Toronto star Auston Matthews , who again was left alone in front of the net. 🙅‍♂️🙅‍♂️🙅‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/opNdpnDRw5 — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 22, 2026 Bjorkstrand got the Rangers even 2:37 into the second period after another breakdown by the Toronto defense. Justin Dowling drove down the right side, cut to the front of the net and swiped the puck at Bobrovsky as he was falling. Gavin McKenna, the first player taken in the 2026 NHL Draft, didn’t stay with Bjorkstrand, who was left all alone and quickly put the puck into the net. Garand and Gavrikov preserved the tie less than a minute later. Marchenko led a 2-on-1 rush, but Garand stopped his rocket from the right circle. The rebound came to Morgan Rielly, who fired toward what looked like an open net — only to have Gavrikov deflect the puck into the netting. The Rangers took their first lead of the night at 6:30 on another deflection goal, this one by Kartye. He was in a pile of bodies in the slot and got a piece of Fox’s wrister from the right point, tipping it down and past Bobrovsky for a 3-2 lead. FOXY THROUGH TRAFFIC + KARTS DEFLECTS IT IN 🤝 pic.twitter.com/qA2U92XBk2 — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 23, 2026 But the Leafs needed just 90 seconds to get even. Duhaime scored his first goal in 66 games when he grabbed his own rebound after a big stop by Garand and banged it past the defenseless goaltender to make it 3-3. The Rangers went more than seven minutes without a shot on goal after Taylor Raddysh ’s long wrister at 9:33, though both Pavel Dorofeyev and J.T. Miller hit posts during that stretch. But the Leafs began controlling play in the later stages of the second period, forcing Garand to make another big stop on Matthews and disrupt William Nylander enough on a breakaway to lift the puck over the crossbar. The Rangers entered the game second in the NHL in penalty killing at 94.1 percent, but Toronto capitalized on the game’s first power play to take the lead with 51 seconds remaining in the period. With Lafreniere off for hooking, Garand made a save on Marchenko’s high shot from the slot but couldn’t control the rebound. Marchenko found it and knocked it in to put the Leafs ahead 4-3 after two periods. Neither team converted on a power-play opportunity early in the third period; however, the Leafs seemed to be in charge as the period passed the halfway mark. Garand kept it a one-goal game when he robbed Cowan with just over 6:30 remaining, and Lafreniere tied it less than a minute later with his long shot through traffic. Garand nearly got the Rangers a point with two more big saves, but Stetcher’s goal spoiled those hopes and triggered an eruption from the crowd of 18,782. item.title: Canucks’ Elias Pettersson Passes Alex Edler For Eighth All-Time In Power-Play Points, Enters Franchise's Top-10 In Power-Play Goals
item.description: Vancouver Canucks forward Elias Pettersson has collected two more franchise milestones. With a goal on the power play against the Detroit Red Wings, Pettersson registered his 178th power-play point, passing Alex Edler for eighth all-time in franchise history. The goal also puts him in sole-possession of 10th all-time in power-play goals. Pettersson has gotten the 2026–27 season off to a hot start, scoring four goals and eight assists. In Vancouver’s 9–7 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on October 1, he claimed sole-possession of ninth all-time in franchise history in goals scored. The game after, a 4–1 win against the Calgary Flames on October 3, Pettersson passed Edler for eighth all-time in assists by a Canuck with his 311th. Pettersson’s next power-play goal milestone isn’t too far away, as former captain Horvat currently sits at ninth all-time with 67 goals scored on the power play. After him is Pavel Bure, whose 69 power-play goals as a Canuck put him at eighth in franchise history. Also ahead of Pettersson on this list is teammate Brock Boeser, who is currently tied with Todd Bertuzzi for fifth in club history with 79. In terms of power-play points as a whole, Pettersson is now only four points away from passing Stan Smyl for seventh all-time. item.title: Kings edge Islanders 3-2 on Clarke goal in overtime
item.description: Oct 22, 2026; Elmont, New York, USA; Los Angeles Kings defenseman Drew Doughty (8) skates against the New York Islanders during the second period at UBS Arena. NEW YORK -- The Kings finally won a game two nights ago to start their four-game road trip and they continued that spirit on Long Island. It was the Artemi Panarin show – plus overtime help from Brandt Clarke on Thursday night as Los Angeles downed the New York Islanders 3-2 as Darcy Kuemper made 41 saves for his second straight victory. Clarke scored at 2:43 of overtime, his second goal this season. Panarin opened the scoring at 5:51 of the first, beating Islanders backup netminder Semyon Varlmov from a sharp angle. The veteran sharpshooter scored again at 16:37, his sixth goal this season, to give the visitors a 2-0 lead into first intermission. Panarin, who turns 35 on Oct. 30, has scored all five Kings road games. Luc Robitaille was the previous Los Angeles player with a such a streak – in October 1999. Panarin joined the Kings in a late season trade from the New York Rangers and scored his first goal for Los Angeles against the Islanders in a 5-3 home win on March 5. Considering his seven seasons as a scoring machine for the Rangers, the Russian forward was booed loudly by the UBS crowd when his name was announced after both goals. In 43 career regular-season games against the Islanders, Panarin has 52 points (21 goals and 31 assists) giving him the second-highest average points per game among active NHLers to play the Islanders at least 40 times. Only Sidney Crosby has a better average per game. The Kings had a golden chance to take a three-goal lead at 10:59 of the middle period when Adrian Kempe was awarded a penalty shot but he was denied by Varlamov. The Islanders solved Keumper when rookie Victor Eklund scored at 16:37 of the second. Defenseman Matthew Schaefer, last season's Calder Trophy winner, then tied the contest with his first goal this season at 7:06 of the third. The Kings were 1-4-2 coming off Tuesday's 5-2 win at Washington in which Panarin had a goal and two assists. Los Angeles entered the contest with a 9-0-1 mark in their last 10 visits to Long Island and they kept that streak going as well. The game also marked the New York-area return for former Rangers and Islanders coach Peter Laviolette, who took over behind the Kings bench last summer. Laviolette coached the Rangers for two seasons before he was let go after New York missed the playoffs in 2024-25. The 61-year-old Laviolette was behind the Islanders bench at the start his coaching career more than two decades ago.

item.title: Cyclones drop third straight match
item.description: Iowa State forward Megan Walters (5) moves with the ball under pressure from Lailah Benz (21) of Kansas State. | Iowa State Athletics Despite 12 saves from goalkeeper Eme McClenahan and holding the majority of possession, Iowa State suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to Big 12 rival Kansas State Thursday night at the Cyclone Sports Complex. The Cyclones (4-8-4, 0-6-2 Big 12) conceded the match’s only goal in the 24th minute when Kansas State forward Rilyn Rintoul converted an assist from substitute Adelle Francis at the 23:24 mark. Goalkeeper Maddie Sibbing recorded three saves across 90 minutes to preserve the clean sheet for the Wildcats (6-6-4, 1-6-1 Big 12). McClenahan anchored a heavy defensive workload for Iowa State, stopping 12 of the 14 shots on target she faced while the Cyclones defense added a goal-line team save in the opening half. Kansas State outshot Iowa State 20-9 overall, launching 13 second-half shot attempts to keep the pressure on the Cyclones’ back line. Iowa State controlled 53% of total possession and earned a 6-3 advantage in corner kicks, including owning 58% of possession during a competitive opening 45 minutes. Defender Breezie Brewer led Iowa State’s attacking efforts with four total shots. Midfielder Lucy Froitzheim generated Iowa State’s best late scoring opportunity in the 88th minute, but her attempt on target was gathered by Sibbing. The physical conference matchup produced 17 total fouls—12 against Kansas State—and featured yellow cards to Iowa State defender Danica Lunceford in the 19th minute and midfielder Allison Charleston in the 72nd minute. An announced crowd of 268 attended the contest, which lasted 1 hour and 57 minutes under referee Jorge Luna Hernandez.

item.title: Hannah Einbinder hits critics with sharp message amid Jalen Hurts blood clot diagnosis
item.description: Hannah Einbinder hits critics with sharp message amid Jalen Hurts blood clot diagnosis appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Hannah Einbinder is making sure those who have a problem with the Philadelphia Eagles or Jalen Hurts should come directly to her. Einbinder took to Instagram this week following Hurts’ diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli, in which the blood clot was in his lower leg and traveled to both of his lungs. “Shut your a– up if you have something bad to say about him and if you have a problem with jalen you have a problem with ME,” Einbinder posted to her Instagram Story on Monday, October 19. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Einbinder made a separate post praising the Eagles quarterback and everything he’s done for the city of Philadelphia. She also agreed with his stance on not going to the White House visit when the Eagles won the Super Bowl in 2025, as well as leading with his faith, among other things. “Jalen,” the Hacks star began with several crying emojis. “We love you so much not only because you’re so talented but because of who you are,” she shared via her Story. “Jalen donated air conditioning units to all the public schools in philly. He has an all female management team and when the eagles won the he refused to go to the white house. I love him so much he speaks in riddles and ancient proverbs GOD protect this man.” Einbinder is diehard Eagles fan and has gone viral several times for her devotion to the Philly football team. When she won Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series for her role as Ava Daniels in Hacks, she yelled “Go Birds!” during her 2025 Emmys acceptance speech. “Go Birds, F*** ICE and Free Palestine” – Hannah Einbinder during her #EMMYs speech pic.twitter.com/k8H6LdKnL6 — Film Updates (@FilmUpdates) September 15, 2025 She then again went viral back in March, the actress claimed that she was a part of a “cult” as she declared her devotion to the Eagles. “Tell me what’s the closest in your estimation to an actual cult?” The reporter then gave the Emmy winner the choices of: competitive cheerleading, improv, or being a Philadelphia Eagles fan. The Rolling Stone Studio at #SXSW : Hannah Einbinder Hannah Einbinder tells Rolling Stone she equates being an @Eagles fan to being in a cult. "I should've said I AM in a cult." pic.twitter.com/uQN0nV5aph — Rolling Stone (@RollingStone) March 18, 2026 “Certainly, the last one there,” she said, confirming her choice of Eagles fan to be close to a cult. “I should have said I am in a cult.” As for Hurts, he is most likely done for the rest of the season given his recent diagnosis. The Eagles will be hosting the Dallas Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26 at 8:15 p.m. ET. Related: Deion Sanders reveals ultimatum for Karrueche Tran if he pays for cosmetic surgery Related: Charles Barkley puts Troy Aikman on blast for being a big baby about Joe Buck situation

item.title: Watch Bears pay incredible tribute to Mike Ditka before TNF vs. Patriots
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Photo By USA TODAY Sports Watch Bears pay incredible tribute to Mike Ditka before TNF vs. Patriots appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL world lost a legendary figure in former Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, who passed away earlier this month at the age of 86. Tributes poured in from all over the football community for Ditka, from current Bears coach Ben Johnson to former Bears player Jim Harbaugh. The Bears had also shared an official statement on Ditka’s passing , but they had been unable to pay tribute to the deceased coach at Soldier Field since they had not had a home game there in the last two weeks. That finally changed on Thursday night, when the Bears hosted the New England Patriots. With several fans dressed up as Ditka with his trademark sunglasses, mustache, and sweater vest, the Bears honored him with a touching moment of silence. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bears hold a moment of silence for the late Mike Ditka 🙌❤️ (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/qrISykanWf — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 23, 2026 Ditka was the Bears’ head coach for 11 seasons, from 1982-1992. He finished with a record of 106-62 and led the Bears to a Super Bowl championship in the 1985 season. Before his outstanding coaching career, Ditka was an accomplished player in his own right. He was taken fifth overall by the Bears in the 1961 NFL Draft. During his rookie campaign, he became the first tight end to top 1,000 yards receiving in a season as he went on to win Rookie of the Year. He went on to win the 1963 NFL Championship with the Bears. He also played on the Dallas Cowboys’ Super Bowl VI championship team. After retiring, Ditka became the first tight end enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988. He would then go on to broadcasting, serving as color commentator on NBC and studio analyst at ESPN. Related: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel set to snap bonkers 27-year streak on TNF vs. Bears Related: Bears’ perfect Riq Woolen trade offer to Eagles before NFL trade deadline

item.title: Player Grades: Cavs at Sixers – A tough debut for Peyton Watson
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 22: Joel Embiid #21 and Jaylen Brown #7 of the Philadelphia 76ers defend a shot from guard Peyton Watson #8 of the Cleveland Cavaliers during the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images As much as things change, they stay the same. The Cleveland Cavaliers opened the new season with a performance that was eerily similar (and equally as deflating) to their Game 1 loss to the New York Knicks in May. Let’s unpack this. As always, grades are based on our usual expectations for each player. Player of the game Mario Hezonja 10 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists , 2 steals If there is a single thing I can leave this game feeling encouraged about — it was Mario Hezonja. Hezonja looks like he belongs. His added strength allows him to be a mismatch-beater in the post, putting Philly into a bind anytime they switched a smaller player onto him. Hezonja is a skilled finisher and a crafty playmaker. This makes him a great option to have on their bench. Mario Hezonja with a pick six! His first stint back in the NBA has been great pic.twitter.com/60H3zi6ubw — Tony Pesta (@Tony_Pesta) October 22, 2026 Defensively, Hezonja kept up with Philly’s pace (until the wheels came off around him). His isolation defense on Jaylen Brown was a highlight. So was this pick-six. He also had a pair of surgical post-ups to end the third quarter that gave me life. Grade: B+ Passed the Class Donovan Mitchell 32 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 5 turnovers There was a lot to like about Mitchell’s first half. He scored 22 points and only missed two shots. His dynamic scoring gave Cleveland a massive lead that should have been enough to coast to victory. It wasn’t. And Mitchell’s turnovers (5) didn’t help the Cavs hold on as the lead was slipping. Still, I think Mitchell is the only other player who did enough to keep a passing grade. I’m not saying he passed with flying colors — but an efficient 32 points and 10 rebounds is hard to knock. I don’t think he was the most guilty party in this meltdown. Grade: C+ Missed the mark Peyton Watson 8 points, 1 rebound, 2 assists, 5 turnovers This was not a good showing for Watson. The biggest concern you could have had (his effect on the floor spacing) was a factor right away. Philly began ignoring Watson in the second half. Leaving him open and packing the paint. He responded by clanking an open three-pointer and barreling into traffic. Watson shot 0-3 from downtown and had 5 turnovers. We can see where Watson fits defensively, and it’s beautiful. But they’ll need much more from him offensively to justify this. Grade: F Jarrett Allen 14 points, 7 rebounds Allen was electric to start this game. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images As much as things change, they stay the same. The Cleveland Cavaliers opened the new season with a performance that was eerily similar (and equally as deflating) to their Game 1 loss to the New York Knicks in May. Let’s unpack this. As always, grades are based on our usual expectations for each player. Player of the game Mario Hezonja 10 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists , 2 steals If there is a single thing I can leave this game feeling encouraged about — it was Mario Hezonja. His first stint back in the NBA has been great pic.twitter.com/60H3zi6ubw — Tony Pesta (@Tony_Pesta) October 22, 2026 Defensively, Hezonja kept up with Philly’s pace (until the wheels came off around him). His dynamic scoring gave Cleveland a massive lead that should have been enough to coast to victory. It wasn’t. And Mitchell’s turnovers (5) didn’t help the Cavs hold on as the lead was slipping. Still, I think Mitchell is the only other player who did enough to keep a passing grade. I’m not saying he passed with flying colors — but an efficient 32 points and 10 rebounds is hard to knock. I don’t think he was the most guilty party in this meltdown. Grade: C+ Missed the mark Peyton Watson 8 points, 1 rebound, 2 assists, 5 turnovers This was not a good showing for Watson. The biggest concern you could have had (his effect on the floor spacing) was a factor right away. Philly began ignoring Watson in the second half. Leaving him open and packing the paint. He responded by clanking an open three-pointer and barreling into traffic. Watson shot 0-3 from downtown and had 5 turnovers. We can see where Watson fits defensively, and it’s beautiful. But they’ll need much more from him offensively to justify this. Grade: F Jarrett Allen 14 points, 7 rebounds Allen was electric to start this game. His 14 points in the first half felt massive as the 76ers simply couldn’t contain him. It turns out, the Cavs would help Philly turn the tide in that regard. Allen didn’t score in the second half. He only attempted one shot. Much of this came from the aforementioned floor-spacing issues. You can’t pass the ball into the paint if there are five bodies there. Still, how many times have the Cavs soared to a massive lead by riding the backs of their bigs, only to ignore them down the stretch? I don’t get paid to solve the problem… but I can confidently say the Cavs need to figure this out! Grade: D+ Evan Mobley 18 points, 8 rebounds, 2 assist s I could repeat almost everything I said about Allen here. Mobley was fantastic in the first half, particularly in the second quarter when his outside shot made it feel pointless for the Sixers to even try. But those results were diminishing, and Mobley struggled to hit perimeter shots and create a bucket when given a runway. I’m placing this more on Mobley than anyone else. He has to find a way to avoid scenarios like this if the Cavs are going to be taken as serious threats. Grade: F James Harden 16 points, 3 rebounds, 5 assist s, 6 turnovers Harden was playing fast and loose for most of the night. There was a sequence in the first half where he turned it over on consecutive possessions, topping it off with an airball on the third. He was far from their biggest problem. In fact, his shot-making gave them a fighting chance in the final minutes. But still, your starting point guard can’t have more turnovers than made field goals if you want to win a game. Grade: D+

item.title: ‘Everyone Would Feel Pretty Upset by That’ — Ex-NFL QB Takes Aim at Joe Buck Over Decision To Negotiate ESPN Deal Without Troy Aikman
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have called NFL games for 25 seasons. They began their journey in the broadcast booth with FOX Sports. In 2022, they moved to ESPN together to call Monday Night Football. However, that may change soon. Football fans recently learned that tensions between Buck and Aikman have escalated to alarming levels . Things came to a head during the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills Monday Night Football contest in Week 5, where the veteran broadcasters reportedly got into a heated argument. Much has been said about this incident and the situation between these two broadcasters. After one recent report, a former NFL quarterback aired his issues with Buck’s reported actions leading to this incident. Brady Quinn Unhappy With Joe Buck Amid Troy Aikman Tension On Wednesday, a report came to light that provided more clarity on what’s going on. In May, Buck is said to have gone to ESPN with his agent to hammer out a new contract extension , according to Puck’s Dylan Byers. He did this without Aikman’s knowledge. Buck eventually signed a new six-year contract, which was announced in September. This did not sit well with former NFL quarterback Brady Quinn, who appeared on “2 Pros & A Cup of Joe” on Wednesday, where he took issue with Buck’s decision to go into negotiations without informing his broadcast partner. “At some point, there was a fracture. ESPN is falling out of favor with Troy for whatever reason. And then Joe, behind his back, going and doing the deal without him knowing this. Which, I think, everyone feels pretty upset by that if you were the guy who brought him in the first place,” Quinn said . According to Byers’ reporting, Buck was told that he may have a new broadcast partner beginning in 2027. That was reportedly not a deterrent for the veteran broadcaster, who “accepted the deal almost immediately.” DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More Buck has called NFL games for over 30 seasons. He began his broadcasting career as a radio voice for a minor league affiliate of the St. Louis Cardinals in 1989. In 1994, he made his television debut with FOX Sports, calling MLB and NFL games. Buck has called multiple Super Bowls and nearly 25 World Series in his illustrious broadcasting career. In 2022, he was inducted into the Sports Broadcasting Hall of Fame. Aikman, meanwhile, is a Pro Football Hall of Famer. He was the first overall pick in the 1989 NFL Draft by the Dallas Cowboys. He spent his entire playing career with the Cowboys, winning three Super Bowls. In 2002, he joined Buck in the FOX Sports booth. Initially, this was a three-man booth with Cris Collinsworth. In 2005, Buck and Aikman became a two-man booth. These two broadcasters have an extensive history with one another. It’s certainly unfortunate that things may end in this manner. Hopefully, an amicable resolution can be reached. We’ll see how the latest news impacts the broadcast, with their next Monday Night Footb

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Next in line? Main contenders for the Manchester United hot seat
item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
